content.text: Experienced Family Law Attorneys Serving in San Jose, CA Why experience matters: Family law in California involves emotional, financial, and legal complexities, and having a certified specialist by your side ensures your rights are protected from day one. Whether you’re negotiating the terms of a divorce, designating the terms of child custody, or agreeing on reasonable division of assets, each decision has a profound impact, affecting the family dynamic that may have already been established for years, if not decades. Unfortunately, fully resolving all the aspects of a separation or divorce may take years – not counting any modifications you may need to make at a later time. If you require assistance in any matters of family law, contact the Schoenberg Family Law Group, P.C. We have a compassionate, experienced San Jose, CA Family Law Attorney who has the knowledge and experience necessary to help ease the burden of the litigation process, giving you the peace of mind you truly deserve. San Francisco Your Children Are Our Top Priority for our Family Law Attorneys Determining child custody and visitation rights may be the most emotionally challenging aspect of family law. The Schoenberg Family Law Group, P.C. understands the serious ramifications of custody rights, taking a compassionate approach to any matters of custody. This includes: Determining custody Rights of paternity, including DNA testing Evaluating child support needs Distinguishing “legal” and “physical” custody Ultimately, the safety and health of the children take top priority in all proceedings, and we ensure they receive the attention and support they deserve. During any family law case in San Jose involving children, we put the children first. We use smart legal strategies and compassionate client care to help parents through difficult times. We can answer your questions about child custody, visitation and parenting plans in detail, lending you peace of mind. Through all legal matters, we focus on your child’s best interests including his or her mental, emotional, physical and psychosocial wellbeing. If we do not believe something will be good for your child, we will not recommend it. We stand by our choices and how they impact the families we represent. Through full transparency and a passion for getting it right, we can help you and your child move forward after a divorce, separation, custody battle or another family law case. Our lawyers understand the San Jose & surrounding Bay Area courts and help you make decisions according to the standard of what is in the child’s best interest. Under California Family Code §3011, custody decisions are based on a child’s best interests, including health, safety, and welfare. Our attorneys ensure that every parenting plan aligns with these statutory standards. Our Family Lawyers in San Jose Make Sure Property Division is Fair For You Dividing a couple’s assets may seem fairly straightforward on paper, but in reality, it can be considerably more complicated. The Schoenberg Family Law Group, P.C. is well-versed in all financial matters involved in a divorce or separation, including: Complex property division Retirement portfolios Debts such as loans Spousal support Pre- and postnuptial agreements Business/professional valuations Property division among domestic partners or other unmarried clients We evaluate your financial state and prioritize your needs to protect your financial health even after separation. California is a community property state under Family Code §760, meaning that assets and debts acquired during marriage are generally divided equally unless an exception applies. We Protect Family Rights At the Schoenberg Family Law Group, P.C, we protect the rights spouses have under California law. We help the clients we represent understand their rights, as well as how to exercise them during settlement negotiations and trials. Whether you come to us for assistance with a custody case or domestic violence, we can provide tailored legal advice that suits your unique needs. Our attorneys protect family rights in California at every turn. Parental rights. Each parent has a right to seek custody and visitation during a divorce case. Our lawyers can help you build a strong and convincing case for custody if your case has to go to trial. We can also help you and your ex-spouse work together during mediation to create a parenting plan of your own before a judge has to intervene. Grandparent rights. California law allows grandparents to lawfully have visitation rights with grandchildren in certain situations. If the child’s parents are living apart, have passed away, have divorced or have abandoned the child, grandparents can petition the courts for the legal right to child visitation. Interests of a child. State courts in California put children’s interests above everything else in family law cases. When ruling on a case, a judge will assess which option will provide for the health, safety and welfare of the child. In general, the courts believe children are better off remaining in contact with both parents. No matter what elements or factors your family law case involves, contact a lawyer for assistance. Our attorneys can help you protect any custody, visitation or other legal rights you may have. A lawyer can also help you seek child support payments after a divorce, if applicable. We offer consultations to anyone who needs answers about family laws in San Jose they can trust. Our attorneys regularly represent clients at the Santa Clara County Family Justice Center Courthouse in downtown San Jose, serving families across the Bay Area. Restraining Orders and Domestic Violence in San Jose Our family law attorneys do not only handle divorce and custody cases – we also help clients with issues such as domestic violence and seeking restraining orders. Sadly, many family law cases involve domestic violence. If your spouse physically, verbally or emotionally abused you or your child, we can help you seek a resolution while protecting yourselves from further violence. Our attorneys can handle the process of obtaining a domestic violence restraining order on your behalf. Under California Family Code §6200 et seq., domestic violence restraining orders protect victims from threats, harassment, and abuse. A domestic violence restraining order in California is a court order that can protect victims from abuse or the threat of abuse. It can require the perpetrator to keep a certain distance from you at all times, as well as to halt all communications and interactions with you and your children. If you and the offender still live in the same household it can also force him or her to move out. You have the right to request a protective order if the offender abused you (or threatened to) and is someone you have a close relationship with. If you do not qualify for a domestic violence restraining order, our lawyers may be able to help you obtain a different type of order, such as a civil harassment restraining order. If your family law case involves domestic violence, we can help you present your version of events to the courts. Domestic violence may be a reason for the courts to award you custody instead of your spouse. Although California is a no-fault state, meaning you do not have to prove domestic violence is the reason for the breakup, showing proof of domestic violence or a history of abuse could have certain benefits for you and your family. Learn more during a consultation with our attorneys. San Jose Visitation Rights and Custody Agreements One of the many family law tasks we can help your family with is child custody. Our San Jose family lawyers understand California’s custody laws and how to navigate them on behalf of parents. We can give you the basics and let you know how we may be able to strengthen your claim to custody or visitation. Our attorneys know which factors a judge in California may examine when making a custody determination. Relationships between the child and each parent The lifestyle to which the child is accustomed The child’s connections to their school and community Either parent’s history of addiction, crime or domestic violence The age of the child (and his or her wishes, if old enough) The child’s health and needs Both parents’ abilities to care for the child The two types of custody orders are physical and legal. Physical custody means the child is physically living with you, while legal custody is the parental right to make important decisions for your child. A judge may award you joint or sole custody of your child. Joint custody means you will share physical and/or legal custody with your ex-spouse. A joint custody arrangement often involves one parent with primary custody and the noncustodial parent having the child on specific days only, such as on the weekends. Custody does not automatically go to either one parent or the other in California. If you and your spouse cannot work out a parenting plan on your own or with help from a mediator, a judge will carefully analyze both sides of the case as well as the best interests of the child. The judge will create a custody arrangement or visitation plan according to what he or she believes is best for the child. The judge’s decision will be final unless the circumstances significantly change in the future. “Best interests of the child” refers to legal standards that prioritize a child’s safety, stability, and emotional wellbeing when courts make custody decisions. When You Need Family Law Help in San Jose An attorney is not a necessity for every divorce case in California. The family courts do not require any petitioner or party to hire legal representation. It might be in your best interests to retain a divorce attorney in San Jose, however, if you have a complicated, difficult or high-value case. You may also want to hire a lawyer to protect your rights, or if you find out that your ex-spouse has hired one. A San Jose, California family law lawyer will stand by your side through each phase of the claims process, guiding you toward what will help your case each step of the way. Our attorneys also represent clients in mediation and settlement conferences before the Santa Clara County Family Court, ensuring their interests are protected at every stage.
